title: Users and Authentication on Junos: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Who gets to log in to your router? And what are they allowed to do once they're in? That's users and login classes.

scenes.heading: The security badge
scenes.narration: On your first day, security made you a badge with your name, photo and a chip listing the doors you can open. Every morning, the guard checks it. The badge is a user account. The chip lists your doors. The root badge is special.

scenes.heading: RADIUS vs TACACS+
scenes.narration: There are two main servers for central logins. R A D I U S combines authentication and authorisation in one packet. T A C A C S plus keeps them separate, which gives finer control over commands. RADIUS combines them, and TACACS plus separates them. So TACACS plus can control individual commands. They're not interchangeable.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three misunderstandings. The root account can't be deleted, only its authentication changed. The operator class can also run ping and traceroute. And RADIUS and TACACS plus split the work differently.

items.right: It can run ping and traceroute

items.wrong: RADIUS and TACACS+ are the same

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva Junos users lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Every user needs a login class. The root account can't be deleted. The default order checks the local password first. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva Junos users lab.

points.t: Every user needs a login class
